title: From Boston radio parts to a brand without stores

events.title: A radio-parts store opens
events.text: Theodore and Milton Deutschmann open the first store, according to the brand’s 2020 owner.

events.title: Tandy buys the chain
events.text: Charles Tandy’s company acquires the struggling Boston chain and makes it profitable within two years.

events.title: The TRS-80
events.text: Tandy sells its own personal computer through the stores (year from general knowledge).

events.title: More than 7,000 locations
events.text: Company stores and dealers combined pass 7,000.

events.title: Stock peaks
events.text: Shares trade as high as $79.50, split-adjusted.

events.title: Tandy becomes RadioShack Corporation
events.text: Net income reaches $368.0M, the most in our data.

events.title: 5,289 company stores
events.text: The most the chain ever operated, plus 2,119 dealer outlets.

events.title: Sales peak at $5.08B
events.text: Net income has already fallen to $267.0M.

events.title: CEO resigns over résumé
events.text: David Edmondson steps down after questions about degrees he claimed.

events.title: Julian Day becomes CEO
events.text: He takes over as chairman and chief executive.

events.title: Layoffs by email
events.text: About 400 headquarters employees are told by email that their jobs are gone.

events.title: 505 fewer stores
events.text: Company stores fall from 4,972 to 4,467, the only large cut before bankruptcy.

events.title: “The Shack”
events.text: The company starts calling itself The Shack in advertising.

events.title: James Gooch becomes CEO
events.text: The former CFO is promoted from president.

events.title: First annual loss in our data
events.text: A net loss of $139.4M. The share price falls below $3.

events.title: Joseph Magnacca becomes CEO
events.text: He arrives from Walgreens.

events.title: Out of Target
events.text: All 1,522 Target Mobile centers are closed or handed off by March 31.

events.title: A $400.2M loss
events.text: Equity falls to $206.4M.

events.title: “The ’80s called”
events.text: A Super Bowl ad mocks the company’s own old stores.

events.title: $43.3M in cash
events.text: Down from $908.2M at the end of 2009.

events.title: Chapter 11
events.text: Filed in Delaware with a plan to sell up to 2,400 stores to a Standard General affiliate.

events.title: 1,743 stores sold
events.text: General Wireless buys them; many are co-branded with Sprint. The rest close.

events.title: Second bankruptcy
events.text: General Wireless files for Chapter 11 and starts closing stores.

events.title: Sold to an e-commerce roll-up
events.text: Retail Ecommerce Ventures buys the brands.

events.title: A crypto token
events.text: radioshack.com becomes a waitlist for a cryptocurrency project.

events.title: Unicomer buys the brand
events.text: The Salvadoran retailer acquires the IP in about 70 countries.
